fields.sample_size: two Ecuadorian collaborative water-governance partnerships; network questionnaire to 22 respondents and 30 in-depth interviews with partnership representatives and key informants 2015-2018 (snowball roster until saturation)
fields.effect_estimate: After the 2014-2015 regulations limiting NGO participation in watershed councils, the denser and more centralised network (high trust, resources to subsidise participation, links to other networks, high perceived legitimacy) was resilient, while the more diverse network dependent on external resources could not adjust; the reforms altered social ties and pushed actors to defect or collaborate at the margins of the regulatory space. Two-case network comparison; no statistical effect estimates.
fields.study_design: qualitative comparative case study with social network analysis of two partnerships
fields.section: Full text: Methods (roster, network questionnaire n = 22, 30 interviews); Results; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methods (roster, network questionnaire n = 22, 30 interviews); Results; Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a two-case comparison of Ecuadorian water-governance partnerships' response to the 2014-2015 participation regulations (22 network questionnaires, 30 interviews), read in full text 2026-10-04. The dense, centralised, trust-rich network was resilient; the externally resource-dependent one was not. Two cases.
pdf_note: Ecology and Society 24(1):29 (2019), about 85,000 characters read
notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds n = 22 + 30. Direct evidence on regulatory change (restrictions on NGO participation) as a stressor on governance partnerships.
